title: Q2 Sequenced Private Rollouts: OKR-aligned Delivery Plan and Cutover Runbooks
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Goal: Produce a sequenced, OKR-aligned quarterly roadmap for Private/VPC/on-prem enterprise features that minimizes customer disruption during cutovers and provides validated runbooks for upgrades, KMS/HSM integrations, and rollback strategies.

Scope: Deliver a prioritized list of feature waves (minimum viable feature set for early customers -> broad enterprise readiness) across three pillars: 1) secure connectivity and RBAC hardening, 2) key management and encryption (KMS/HSM integrations + key rotation procedures), 3) upgrade/compatibility runbooks for on-prem agents and private control planes. Include acceptance criteria, staging and canary gating metrics, and a cross-functional stakeholder map.

Success metrics:
- 95% of staged customers pass canary cutover without rollback within two weeks of rollouts.
- Runbooks validated with at least two pilot customers and one internal dry-run.
- Security review completed and closed with remediation backlog < 5 items.
- OKR alignment: Contributes to OKR-PD.1 (Private reliability) and OKR-Sec.2 (Key management compliance).

Deliverables and milestones:
- Draft sequencing and risks (Week 2 of cycle)
- Runbook templates for KMS/HSM, on-prem upgrades, and rollback procedures (Week 4)
- Pilot cutover with two customers and internal dry-run (Week 8)
- Final roadmap approved by Eng/SRE/Security/Product Council (Week 10)

Trade-offs considered:
- Phased wave approach vs. big-bang release: phased reduces blast radius and eases support load but increases coordination complexity and prolongs full enterprise coverage. We recommend phased waves tied to customer segments (pilot -> strategic -> general availability).
- Strict gating (higher confidence) increases time-to-ship; lighter gating increases risk. Proposal: require full security sign-off and SLO-based canary gates before every wave.

Risks and mitigations:
- KMS integration variability across customer KMS vendors: mitigate via a compatibility matrix and a prioritized adapter effort.
- Upgrade failures due to agent/hypervisor differences on-prem: mitigate with expanded test matrix and lightweight rollback hooks.
- Insufficient SRE on-call capacity for concurrent waves: reserve dedicated runbook responders and limit parallel waves.

Stakeholders and reviewers: Product (Liam O'Connor), Engineering (SRE leads: Marco Ruiz), Security (Aisha Patel), Solutions Engineers (Priya Desai), Customer Success (Derek Mills).

Open asks: 2 additional SRE FTEs for April/May runbooks and a small budget (~$25k) for pilot customer test environments.

Artifacts: Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIVATE/Q2+Sequenced+Rollouts (draft), Design sketches: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1q2-private-rollout-designs (mockups), Pilot checklist PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-rollout/pull/128
